sections.text: He who with unclouded vision sees Me as the Lord-God, knows all there is to be known, and always shall worship Me with his whole heart.
Thus, O Sinless One, I have revealed to thee this most mystic knowledge. He who understands gains wisdom and attains the consummation of life.

We had been discussing chapter 15, Purushottama yoga, yoga of the Supreme Purusha. We have heard these terms before in Bhagavad Gita and Vedanta, Purusha and Prakriti. We understood from this discussion that the Prakriti is the manifest.
Anything that which I can see, touch, feel and vouch for its existence is Prakriti, including my thoughts, my ideas. Because other people may not be able to vouch for, I can vouch for it that they exist. Anything that exists in the realm of my perception, feeling in thoughts is a Prakriti.
But that which supports this Prakriti or awareness is the Purusha. I am aware of this Prakriti because I am alive. If I am not alive, this body cannot perceive whether it is day or night.
So that conscious principle in me is a Purusha. Thats what we understood. The Prakriti is changing every minute, every second.
At a micro level, my body. My body has been changing every minute. I may not realize it till I see my pictures from five years ago.
One good thing about these pictures on a website, we never change it. So I have a picture which was taken in 2003 on my website and anywhere else. So when the people come in contact with you in person, they get shocked.
Rajan, you know, look a little different. Well, I never realized it. But other people who say it or when we see our picture, we realize this is constantly changing.
What it was yesterday is not today. So that falls into the category of a perishable things and beings. This body is perishable.
But this body is supported by something which remains constant. This change Im noticing in my body because something remains constant. That constant factor is gauging the change.
I used to look like this. I used to have all dark hair, all my beard was dark. That one who notices the change remains constant.
That the support for this change. Change can only takes place if there is something constant. So in my life, I, the consciousness, I, the awareness is constant.
So when we remember Our childhood memories we dont think that that was something a different person. I remember this happened to me I remember that I remain constant. Everything else about me keeps changing.
So at my micro level, there are two Purushas, two me. One is perishable, which is the body, mind and intellect. One is imperishable, which is the one who is aware of these changes -- the one who is afraid of death. Otherwise, why would I be afraid if there is not someone watching and saying, Looks like this body is going to go out? People ask me all the time now, Rajan, whats your plan? I said, What do you mean, whats my plan? He said, Were talking about retirement. I said, I have no plan, because I feel the way I felt when I started NBG Architecture the very first day.
Im the same person. Youre going to be qualified for Medicare in a couple of months, so Im sure you have some plan. And at that time I started thinking, oh, is that so? Statistically, Indians dont really last longer than somewhere about the early 70s. Thats 65 -- I probably have less than 10 years. If I have less than 10 years, I havent even planned what Im going to do.
Because I never feel old. That I at my level is always imperishable. We started out this chapter by saying that when I think about myself, it seems like my source is somewhere unknown up above, but my life is all here, spread all around.
The same way, now I look at it: when Bhagavan talked about the nature of the Supreme Being, everything that you see, perceive and feel is nothing but my expression. Right now Im only worried about me. Im not worried about whether youre going to retire or she is going to retire or hes going to retire -- what am I going to do? Im also not worried about whether you people will be around when I die.
After I die, Im only worried about what will happen to me. So at my level, Bhagavan said, in this Loka, Dvau Purushau -- there are two Purushas in this world. In my world there are two Purushas.
One which is perishable, that I see. Bhagavan said, nothing that you see is other than me. I only exist and pervade everywhere.
Everything you see, touch, feel and perceive is nothing but my expression -- including the perception of my own body, mind and intellect, which is deteriorating. I cant remember even my employee who has just left me three days ago. She used to work here. Because the memory is not now as good as it used to be. So I see this perishable me, which is also the Purusha.
And I also see the imperishable one who doesnt think about retirement even now. Dvau Imau Purushau -- in this loka of mine, in this world of mine, there are two Purushas. One is perishable, one is imperishable.
Does the world end here for me? Beyond these two, there is a supreme Purusha. Right now that supreme Purusha I really have no connection with. So therefore Im only worried about this Purusha.
The one I feel is imperishable. Whatever I feel is still as young as when I used to be a little child. Bhagawan said that beyond these two there is a Purusha which transcends both the imperishable and perishable.
And the example which we have seen is this room space is imperishable. Room, walls, floor and ceiling is perishable. We are doing some renovation next door.
So we say Ill move this wall here and do this because thats perishable. But we know that the space itself is imperishable. In relationship to the wall, floor and ceiling, this space is imperishable.
But if we remove this walls, floor and ceiling out of the equation, what happens to this imperishable space? Its not even imperishable anymore. If there is no perishable things in this world, the word imperishable means nothing, right? Because it is imperishable compared to perishable thing. Long-lasting battery, short-lasting battery.
Lifetime warranty -- but whose lifetime? The batterys life, or the manufacturers life? Or that companys life? All of our contractors, we ask them we need 10 year warranty or 15 year warranty. 20 years warranty guy gladly give. 5 years from now youll try to call him and say we have problem, we need you to. The phone number is out of service. So the lifetime warranty we get is not your lifetime, its the lifetime of the company.
As long as companies, the warranty is good. But all these things are relative. But if you take the relationship out, what remains is absolute which you cannot really compare in this world.
So this Purusha, one is perishable, this body one is imperishable. Which is conditioned by this body, mind and intellectual. But if you remove the conditioning, what remains is absolute Purusha which is neither perishable nor imperishable but ever existing.
And that Bhagavan said is by nature. So he said Uttamahapuru Sahatu Annyaha Paramatma ITI Udahrutah. We heard the word Paramatma.
What does paramatma means? My atma is imperishable compared to my self. The body, mind, intellect. But if I dont have this body, mind, intellect, that atma is absolute.
Therefore it is param Atma. Not in reference to this. Our idea is that imperishable.
Bhagavad Gita said that Im imperishable. Even if I die, Ill be nil bhatt somewhere. Bhagavan said Paramatma, it will be part of the infinite.
Therefore that supreme being which forms this being as me is a paramatma. Gives a very nice example. Even within a room space there is a pot space.
The space in the coffee cup is room space. The space remains in the room. But when I even remove the room, the whole room space becomes so.
When we take these layers out of identification, this is my mind, this is my body, this is my intellectual. They have their own identity and then I have my identity. The I which is my mind, my body, my intellect.
When you remove in this I, what remains is just an absolute self. My atma, not conditioned by my limitations is Paramatma. Your lokatriyam Avishya Bibhartya via Ishvaraha.
That Paramatma is supporting the three worlds I live in my three worlds. Waking dream and deep sleep. My waking world is different.
My dream world is different and my deep sleep world is different. I, the conditioned self is going through all these three experiences in my life. But the condition self is supported by whom? This room space is bigger, smaller, depending on where I put the walls here.
But supported by what? By the universal space. This is a part of that universal space. Yasmaat Aksharam Atito Aham Aksarat Apicho Uttamah.
Therefore Bhagavans Yasmat Aksharam Adith. This self is even beyond imperishable. This self in me is much greater than this perishable Me.
Thats what we take some solace in learning Bhagavad Gita that even if I die, I will not die. Bhagavan said, but that self is even beyond Aksharaha. Beyond this imperishableness. Imperishable as we have seen is only reference to the perishable.
So lets say my life is hundred years. But there are things here which are 5000 years old. Compared to me, that thing has existing forever.
But this time frame, when we completely remove the scale from our mind, what remains is absolute existence. No past, no present, no future. So Bhagavan said, Yasmat Aksharam Atitah -- beyond imperishable and perishable.
I am even supreme beyond this perishable and imperishable. Atah Asmi Loke Cha Vede Cha Prathitah Purushottamah. We had been hearing this word Purushottama.
What is that Purushottama? He said, because my real nature -- I the Lord, the Ishvara -- and I say Lordship is that which supports my existence. That is my Lord. Thats when we call King a Lord.
Because my existence as the commoner is because of his grace. He allows me to do that. Thats why hes the Lord.
In this case my Lord is him. Because my existence is because of him. Therefore in this world I am called Purushottama in the Vedas.
Purushottama is described in Vedas as the one which is beyond perishable and imperishable. And also the scholars and poets in this world has sung its glory as something beyond perishable and imperishable. And therefore Bhagavan said, I am called Purushottama.
Therefore this chapter was called Purushottama Yoga. Yoga of Purushottama. Right now I am completely yoked with this perishable and imperishable Purusha. I am very aware this is perishable me.
I also know this body is going to die. But I have complete identification with it. I also have some solace because I had been learning Bhagavad Gita for many, many, many years.
That something within me is imperishable. Bhagavan said, but I am Purushottama. I am beyond this perishable and imperishable.
Therefore I am called Purushottama. My own self, when it drops its relationship with this body, mind and intellect, this world, this perception, this feeling, these thoughts -- it becomes Purushottama. Yo Mam Evam Asammudhah Janati Purushottamam -- who knows his self as Purushottama? One who is Asammudhah, one who is undeluded.
We, whether we like it or not, are deluded -- fooled by the illusion that you are different from me and she is different from he. No matter how hard we try, this conditioning is so complete that we will not be able to get out of it. R.
Bhagavan said there is a state for a Gyani to go beyond this illusion or delusion that he sees all the time that his relationship is with the Purushottama and not with this Purusha. Sarva Vid Bhajati Maam Sarva Bhavena Bharata.

The chapter concludes with both a promise and a proclamation. Yo mam evam asammudho janati purushottamam - whoever knows Me thus, without delusion, as the Supreme Person, knows all there is to be known. This is not intellectual knowledge but direct recognition. The word asammudha (undeluded) is key - our usual state is one of delusion, convinced that we are separate individuals competing with other separate individuals. The sage who sees through this illusion recognizes that the same Purushottama that animates his being animates all beings. Such a person, says Krishna, worships Me with his whole being (sarva-bhavena). This is not partial devotion squeezed between other activities, but total orientation of life.
Verse 20 calls this teaching guhyatamam shastram - the most secret of all scriptures. Why secret? Not because it is hidden, but because it can only be understood by a prepared mind. Krishna promises that one who truly understands this becomes wise (buddhiman) and has accomplished all that needs to be accomplished (kritakritya). Imagine that - nothing more to achieve, nothing more to become. This is the consummation of human life. Today, carry this question: What if my deepest identity is not the struggling person I take myself to be, but the Purushottama itself, temporarily playing the role of this individual? How would that change what I pursue, what I fear, and how I treat others who are equally expressions of that same Supreme Person?
